searchText: something broke 🤔 https://etherscan.io/nodetracker It's just an error on etherscan's side. ethernodes.org shows 6000 nodes. Does anyone know if there is research doing network analysis of transactions on Ethereum? I think it would be really cool to see a visual/graphical representation of the network We will add more detail eventually Not what I was really looking for, but this is also useful information. How do you estimate future blocks? Based on mempool https://www.gasprice.io/ check it out we also show gas price of pending txs I get how you can look in the mempool to see what transactions are waited to be executed, but I meant how do you know how to order them? what year is this from? https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Visualization-of-the-Transaction-Value-in-the-Bitcoin-Network_fig35_296700474 2016 looks about right lol I only included the photo to help illustrate what I was looking for I know people are doing it on a small scale I saw a paper about the circulation of nft sale funds, that it's basically going in circles https://etherscan.io/chart/address Based off of this chart, if someone wanted to create a network visualization graph, they would somehow have to represent ~180M nodes <@354681205842771973> good question for Alex 😂 https://blockchair.com/ethereum/charts/total-transaction-count ~180M nodes and ~1.4B edges We evaluate the entire txpool just as it was a single block And the transactions are ordered by the Geth miner code Which means that our data provides you the best and the most precise visualization of the transaction queue Gasprice.io is super advanced compared to other gpo’s I like the lowest base fee last 30 days. Would be nice to have more of that. Maybe last 7 days and 24 hours? <@!354681205842771973> Reply to alwx not me 😂😂 Have you seen the Cosmos map / zone explorer? Something like that for ethereum would be amazing Check this out man (for ATOM though not ETH) — https://mapofzones.com/?testnet=false&period=24&tableOrderBy=totalIbcTxs&tableOrderSort=desc Just posting out of curiosity / given it seemed relevant for data visualizations. I was looking into maybe doing something similar to map the ethereum network + have visualizations for liquidity & messaging flows Haven't heard of that I thought about creating a visual network graph for Ethereum for every transaction starting from block 0 😳 But I would need access to an archive node and a lot of computing resources to hold all that data Erigon’s archive nodes are “small”, at 1.6TB! Maybe someone can form a DAO and rent an entire data center That's not bad I'll check it out, thanks 🙂
